## Team completes Bradley-to-Fountain segment ahead of schedule, as part of the Midway-to-Kelker progressive design-build program


Construction is off to a successful start in Colorado Springs, Colo., as Great Southwestern Construction (Great Southwestern), an MYR Group subsidiary, completed the first transmission line segment of a portfolio of electrical transmission and substation projects for Colorado Springs Utilities (Springs Utilities).


Planning for the[Midway-to-Kelker](https://www.csu.org/current-projects/midway-kelker-transmission-line) portfolio began in 2021, which includes dismantling about 18 miles of existing 115kV transmission line and constructing a new, 115kV and 230kV two-circuit line on steel monopole structures in the southern corridor of the city. Some sections of the new transmission line will cross wetlands and Interstate 25. A separate transmission circuit was later added bringing the total transmission to nearly 25 miles. Multiple substations will be upgraded to accommodate the added 230kV line.


Springs Utilities Project Manager Ryne Solberg explained that the overall project is necessary to meet the community and utility’s growing power needs. The utility aims to increase capacity to allow for import and export of power to the Southwest Power Pool, a regional transmission organization, to ensure those needs are met now and in the future.


The improvements to their transmission line and substations will increase the amount of electricity that can be delivered to their system and harden structures to improve reliability and resiliency for their customers.


“A lot of these structures are in wildfire risk areas and wind areas,” Solberg said. “We’re working to mitigate those risks by upgrading to steel monopole structures.”


### **Early Delivery of the First Transmission Segment**


Outage constraints limit when electrical transmission upgrades can be performed, confining them mainly to brief windows in the fall and spring when the community’s power usage loads are lower. It also means completion is essential, so that the line can be reenergized to deliver power again.


The portfolio’s transmission work was divided into several segments with the Bradley-to-Fountain segment being rebuilt first. Great Southwestern began construction in December 2025.


The roughly four-mile section of line stretches through a busy corridor including the Fountain Creek Regional Trail and alongside Interstate 25 (I-25) across from the entrance to the Fort Carson Army Base.


Throughout the project, the team coordinated extensively with Springs Utilities, the Colorado Department of Transportation (CDOT), El Paso County representatives, and the public.


Great Southwestern removed 33 existing structures and constructed 35 new steel monopole structures, pulled in all new conductor wire for both circuits, sagged it at extreme tensions to mitigate east to west wind vibration, and installed shield wire to protect the system from lightning and optical ground wire (OPGW) to transmit high speed data.


They also succeeded in keeping the public safe even when individuals disregarded posted signs and physical barriers. Because the transmission line crosses the public path in multiple locations, the utility and county announced temporary closures of a portion of the Fountain Creek Regional Trail. Great Southwestern reinforced these measures by installing fencing and prominent “trail closed” signage. Despite these precautions, some members of the public still entered the closed trail and encroached on the active work area.


To manage the public, Great Southwestern posted flaggers with radios in strategic locations while work was being performed. The flaggers required members of the public to stop and wait while they contacted the transmission wire pulling crew to briefly hold work while the person crossed safely.


To keep work progressing when a mechanical issue arose with a wire puller just two weeks before scheduled reenergization, Great Southwestern crews pivoted to install insulators while an MYR Group mechanic fixed the puller. It was back up and running within a day. Wire pulling resumed and construction was completed several days ahead of schedule and without any safety incidents. The Bradley to Fountain section was reenergized on April 20.


Collaborative planning between the utility, Great Southwestern and an engineering partner began long before construction and helped set it up for success. Springs Utilities has been very pleased with Great Southwestern’s work so far.


“Their construction crews are remarkable. They know when they are going to encounter an obstacle and try to get ahead of it,” Solberg said.


Operations Manager Mack Smith credited the project team’s excellent upfront planning for the project, open communication, and planning and adaptation by field personnel for the successful completion of the Bradley-to-Fountain segment. Crews displayed excellent teamwork and worked long hours to deliver this important project for the customer.


“Everyone at every level did a good job,” Smith said.


Their apprentices gained valuable experience on the project including how to properly dead-end wire, the best practices for wire pulling, how to inspect rigging, set steel monopoles, and most importantly the importance of grounding and bonding procedures to conduct work safely.


“Speaking with them now, they’re very happy and you can see they are more confident and excited for the next job,” Smith added.


### **Bringing Construction Expertise into Design and Planning with Progressive Design-Build**


Great Southwestern won the rebuild Midway to Kelker project portfolio again as a progressive design-build project portfolio.


Progressive design-build is a collaborative project delivery approach in which the owner, engineering partner, and construction partner work together from the earliest stages of project development. Unlike traditional delivery methods — where design is completed before a contractor is ever engaged — progressive design-build brings construction expertise into the design process itself.


For Midway-to-Kelker, Great Southwestern serves as the prime contractor and main point of contact. This ensures engagement in all aspects of project planning, design and execution from the start through partnership with a design and engineering firm in collaboration with Springs Utilities.


Great Southwestern was able to provide construction expertise during design to improve constructability and equipment access and procured certain materials early to protect the customer from price escalation.


This method can ultimately result in faster project delivery because the design and construction phases overlap and the construction team already knows the project inside and out.


Now that Bradley-to-Fountain is complete, Great Southwestern will turn to the Fountain substation upgrades in the fall and begin the next segment of transmission work in early 2027.
